**Why join us?

**Muuto is rooted in the Scandinavian design tradition characterized by enduring aesthetics, functionality, craftsmanship and an honest expression. By expanding this heritage with forward-looking materials, techniques and bold creative thinking, our ambition is to deliver new perspectives on Scandinavian design.

We are looking for a commercially minded and analytical Category Manager to strengthen our global supplier network, drive category performance, and support the continued growth of our business.

As Category Manager, you will play a key role in developing and managing supplier relationships, improving operational performance, and ensuring that our supply chain remains scalable, resilient, and aligned with Muuto’s ambitious growth plans.

**Key Responsibilities

**You will be responsible for a portfolio of suppliers and product categories, working closely with Product Development, Sustainability, and Commercial teams.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Developing and executing category strategies aligned with business objectives

• Managing supplier relationships, negotiations, and performance reviews

• Driving continuous improvements in lead time, delivery performance, quality, and cost

• Identifying and implementing sourcing opportunities and risk mitigation plans

• Leading supplier development initiatives and supporting dual sourcing strategies

• Monitoring KPIs and using data-driven insights to improve category performance

• Supporting new product introductions from design to market launch

• Collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders to optimize supply chain performance

• Ensuring supplier compliance with Muuto standards, sustainability requirements, and business processes

• Driving transparency and reporting across supplier and category performance

**WHO ARE YOU?

**We imagine that you have:

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business, Procurement, or a related field

• 5+ years of experience within Category Management, Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, or Supply Chain

• Strong negotiation and stakeholder management skills

• Experience managing international suppliers and complex supply chains

• Strong analytical capabilities and experience working with KPIs and performance management

• Commercial understanding combined with a collaborative and relationship-focused approach

• The ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution

• Excellent communication skills in English

• Experience from furniture, design, consumer goods, or manufacturing industries will be considered an advantage.

**WE OFFER

**At Muuto, you become part of an international design company where creativity, collaboration, and entrepreneurship are part of everyday life.

You will get:

• A key role in shaping supplier and category strategies

• Exposure to a global supplier network

• Close collaboration with design, product development, and commercial teams

• Opportunities for professional and personal development

• A dynamic, informal, and ambitious work environment

• The chance to contribute to one of the strongest design brands in the Scandinavian industry

You will report to the Supply Chain Manager, and the position is expected to start as soon as possible.

To learn more about Muuto, our products, and our designers, please visit Muuto.com.

If you are interested, please upload your CV and application via the link as soon as possible.

**Who We Hire?

**At Muuto, our mission is to deliver new perspectives on Scandinavian design. We are an international team of ambitious and passionate people - all driven by the desire to expand on the Scandinavian design tradition with a forward-looking, creative and honest approach. We are looking for qualified applicants representing a wide range of backgrounds and abilities who share this same mindset. Individuals who wish to actively contribute and bring their opinion to the table. Individuals who would like to bring a wealth of new perspectives to our company.

That is why we are always keen to hear from talented people who wish to join our company - regardless of gender identity, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, racial identity, religious belief and disability status. We are committed to equal opportunity employment.

To learn more about Muuto, our products and designers, please visit www.muuto.com

MillerKnoll complies with applicable disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and employees with disabilities. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact MillerKnoll Talent Acquisition at careers_help@millerknoll.com.

Includes activities linked to new product development and technical improvement of existing products and components. • Strong background in electronic hardware development with demonstrated experience in power electronics.

• Working knowledge of analog and digital electronics and the integration of complete electronic systems.

• Experience with laboratory testing, troubleshooting, debugging, and verification of electronic hardware.

• Experience supporting manufacturing activities, including root cause analysis, corrective actions, and implementation of hardware improvements.

**Desired Characteristics

• Experience supporting products in production environments and working with manufacturing, quality, sourcing, and suppliers to resolve technical issues.

• Familiarity with ECR/ECO processes, design transfer, production launch, and lifecycle management activities.

• Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal and leadership skills. Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems. Established project management and cross-functional collaboration skills.

The role

We are looking for a senior hardware/product development engineer with strong experience taking physical products from prototype through engineering validation and into manufacturing.

You will work directly with the founder and take ownership of the physical architecture of Dreamspire.

This is not primarily a firmware role and it is not a pure industrial-design role.

We need someone who can look at a prototype and systematically turn it into a product.

You should be comfortable moving between:

• mechanical engineering

• electronics integration

• manufacturing

• prototyping

• reliability

• assembly

• suppliers

• cost

• compliance

• user experience

A large part of the work will initially be hands-on.

Your first mission

Your first objective will be to create a clear Dreamspire Product Architecture V1.

You will examine the existing prototype, identify its weaknesses and determine how we should build the next generation of the system.

This includes answering questions such as:

• Which prototype mechanisms are suitable for a real product?

• What needs to be redesigned?

• Which components should be custom versus off-the-shelf?

• How should cameras, lighting, electronics and mechanical systems be integrated?

• How do we make assembly simple and repeatable?

• What are the major reliability risks?

• What manufacturing processes should we use?

• What should the production BOM look like?

• What needs tooling?

• What can initially be produced in low volume?

• What compliance and certification work will be required?

• How do we move from one prototype to 10, 100 and eventually thousands of units?

The objective is not to rush into manufacturing.

The objective is to progressively remove technical and manufacturing risk until the product is ready.

Responsibilities

You will:

• Audit the existing Dreamspire hardware and mechanical architecture.

• Design and build improved prototype generations.

• Own mechanical design and product engineering.

• Integrate cameras, PCBs, lighting, power, cabling, connectors and sensors into the physical product.

• Design enclosures, mounts, mechanisms and structural components.

• Define tolerances and mechanical interfaces.

• Design for manufacturing and assembly — DFM/DFA.

• Reduce part count, assembly complexity and manufacturing cost.

• Select appropriate materials and production methods.

• Decide when to use CNC, sheet metal, 3D printing, injection molding or other processes.

• Work with PCB/electronics engineers where specialist electrical work is required.

• Develop production BOMs and cost estimates.

• Source and evaluate components and suppliers.

• Communicate directly with prototype houses and manufacturers.

• Design test fixtures and production test procedures.

• Establish reliability and lifecycle testing.

• Help define EVT, DVT and PVT stages.

• Identify CE, EMC, electrical safety and other relevant compliance requirements.

• Help design the system for serviceability and repair.

• Help prepare Dreamspire for small pilot production and eventually mass production.

What we are looking for

The most important requirement is:

You have personally helped ship real physical products.

Ideally, you have taken products through several stages of:

prototype → engineering validation → manufacturing → production → customer

You should have strong practical experience with several of the following:

• Mechanical engineering

• Mechatronics

• Consumer electronics

• Product development

• DFM / DFA

• CAD

• Injection-molded plastic parts

• CNC and rapid prototyping

• Electronics packaging

• PCB integration

• Cameras / optical systems

• Sensors

• Motors or electromechanical systems

• Tolerance analysis

• Supplier management

• BOM optimization

• Production testing

• Reliability testing

• Manufacturing ramp-up

You should be comfortable physically building, modifying and debugging prototypes rather than only designing them.

Particularly relevant backgrounds

Experience from products such as these would be especially relevant:

• Consumer electronics

• Robotics

• Smart-home products

• Interactive toys

• Gaming hardware

• IoT products

• Camera systems

• Medical or laboratory devices

• Small electromechanical products

Experience working in a startup or small product-development team is a major advantage.

What we are not looking for

This is probably not the right role if your experience is primarily:

• Arduino hobby projects

• Pure firmware development

• PCB design without product/mechanical ownership

• Industrial design without engineering responsibility

• CAD work without manufacturing experience

• Large-company engineering where manufacturing and suppliers were handled entirely by other teams

We are looking for someone who understands the whole physical product.

How you work

You should enjoy environments where the product is still evolving.

You should be able to say:

“This prototype mechanism works, but it will not survive production.”

or:

“We can remove these five components if we redesign this assembly.”

or:

“Don’t spend money tooling this yet — we need to validate this part first.”

We want someone who challenges assumptions and prevents expensive mistakes rather than simply implementing specifications.

Working with the founder

You will work closely with the founder, who currently develops the software, computer-vision systems, embedded systems and game concepts.

You will therefore have considerable influence over the architecture of the product.

The expectation is that you become the technical owner of the physical Dreamspire platform, while working closely with software and game development.

If the collaboration works well, the role could evolve into something resembling:

Head of Hardware / Head of Product Engineering

as Dreamspire grows.

Location

The role is based around Copenhagen.

Much of the work can be done remotely, but during prototype development we expect regular hands-on work with the physical Dreamspire system.

Candidates elsewhere in Denmark or the Øresund region are welcome if they can work regularly in Copenhagen.

Relocation support is not available at this stage.

Employment

We are open to:

• Full-time employment

• 3–4 days/week

• An initial senior consulting/fractional arrangement that can develop into a permanent role

For a strong permanent candidate, expected salary is approximately:

65,000–75,000 DKK/month + pension, depending on experience.

Exceptional candidates with significant consumer-product leadership experience may be above this range.

Why this role is interesting

Dreamspire is not another incremental electronics product.

The aim is to create an entirely new category of tabletop gaming platform and then build multiple games on top of it.

The fundamental question is:

Can we create something with the physical presence and social experience of a board game, but with systems and mechanics that were previously only practical in video games?

A large part of whether that succeeds depends on making the hardware disappear into the experience.

That is the problem we want you to help solve.

How to apply

Email jobs@dreamspire.dk with your CV and a few lines about the physical products you have helped ship. We read every application and use it only to assess it; see how we handle your data.

Strong experience with AWS (EKS, RDS, S3, CloudFront, IAM, etc.) and security best practices.

jobs.description:
Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The Opportunity

Veo's security surface is unusual. We train models on-premise on dedicated GPU infrastructure, run the product across AWS and GCP, and operate a fleet of tens of thousands of cameras deployed at clubs and venues worldwide. That is a scope most SaaS security engineers never touch: physical devices in the field, heavy on-prem compute, and multi-cloud production, all in one role.

We are forming a Security Enablement Team that makes it easier for every engineering and IT team at Veo to build, ship, and operate secure systems. You will own the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet, partnering with the teams that own these systems so security is built in from the start. As an enablement function, the team does not run these systems day to day. We build the paved roads, tooling, and patterns that let the owning teams operate securely by default.

You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across infrastructure, network, and workforce identity security, and rolling out the first paved roads for a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen), workforce identity and access, and drift checks for cloud configuration and network rules. You'll have direct impact on how 100+ engineers, and every Veo employee, work securely across our offices and clouds.

What You Will Do

You'll join the Security Enablement Team and focus on the infrastructure and cloud security slice, where office networks, data center networks, and employee access to product systems meet. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership of the team's work, pair on complex problems, and rotate responsibilities. The systems themselves stay with the owning teams, and our job is to make those teams successful.

• Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for our office and data center networks and the VPN that connects them, as part of the network security direction the team sets together. Day-to-day operation and firewall changes stay with the team that owns the network

• Build patterns and tooling for secure cross-site connectivity and endpoint security posture that IT can adopt and run, in a way that supports how Veo engineers actually work

• Build the patterns and automation for workforce identity and access, including SSO hygiene, MFA enforcement for employees, and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows for access to product systems, with IT owning the day-to-day operation

• Build automated checks that surface drift in cloud configuration and network rules, so the owning teams get a signal and can act on it

• Act on infrastructure and network findings from external penetration tests, routed through the team's shared intake, with the owning teams driving remediation

• Build the first version of cross-cutting capabilities, such as the cross-site VPN or the drift checks, then hand each one to a long-term owner with a written transition that covers the runbook, ownership, and escalation path

• Partner with GRC to build evidence pipelines for IT and access-related controls that produce auditable output without manual follow-up

• Run office hours where IT, platform, and product teams can get a network or access review

As the team matures, you'll help shape how Veo's network and identity stack evolves across our offices and clouds as the company grows.

What You Could Bring

This role deliberately sits where IT, cloud, and security meet. You do not need to be world class at all three. You are strong in one or two and comfortable operating across the rest.

You likely have several years of experience at that intersection. That tends to show up in several of the following:

• Solid IT fundamentals: networking, identity, endpoint posture, MFA, and SSO at production scale

• Cloud infrastructure experience: hands-on work on at least one of GCP or AWS, including IAM, networking, and basic Terraform-style IaC

• Workforce identity and access: hands-on experience with SSO and identity providers (Okta, Google Workspace) and clean joiner, mover, and leaver flows

• A security mindset layered on that IT and cloud depth: you instinctively look for misconfigurations, drift, and bad access patterns, without needing to be a dedicated security specialist

• Cross-context comfort: you can work on an office network problem and a product cloud problem in the same week without context-switching pain

• Platform-as-product mindset: you've built internal tooling that real teams adopt, with guard rails built into the tools people already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured impact

• Comfort handing work back to a long-term owner once the build phase is done

• Collaboration: you work through discussion and feedback, share context effectively, and write things down.

Nice to have: VPN solutions at scale (Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, WireGuard), endpoint management tooling, and audit log pipelines.

How We Work

You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on most of it but not all of it, apply anyway. People who span IT, cloud, and security are rare, and we do not expect every box ticked. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

**Product Management at Dalux, Innovating the Construction Industry

**Dalux continues to grow rapidly, and we’re looking for a Product Manager to help shape the future of BIM and make complex building information accessible and useful to everyone in construction.

As a Product Manager at Dalux, you’ll operate at the intersection of customer needs, technology, and business strategy. You’ll take ownership of the product roadmap and collaborate closely with Product Design and Development teams to deliver intuitive, high-performing BIM experiences.

You’ll play a key role in evolving how our users view, navigate, understand, and collaborate around building models. Combining an understanding of BIM, UI/UX, and computer graphics, you’ll help turn complex technical capabilities into tools that work effortlessly for our users.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Product Discovery: Evaluate and prioritize new product opportunities, balancing user value, technical feasibility, and business impact.

• Customer Insights: Work closely with users to understand their BIM workflows, uncover pain points, and translate feedback into meaningful product improvements.

• User Experience: Collaborate with Product Design to make complex BIM interactions intuitive, from navigating 3D models to finding and understanding building information.

• BIM and Visualization: Work with engineers on model visualization and interaction, balancing visual quality, responsiveness, and performance when handling large and complex building models.

• Cross-functional Collaboration: Align with engineers, designers, and fellow product managers to deliver cohesive experiences across Dalux products.

• Feature Ownership: Lead new features from discovery and definition through development, delivery, and validation with users.

• Product Strategy: Help define the direction of BIM at Dalux, identifying opportunities and deciding where we should invest to deliver the greatest value.

**What To Expect As a Daluxian

**At Dalux, we offer a creative, collaborative, and supportive environment where your ideas make an impact. Here’s what you can look forward to as part of our team:

• A central location in Copenhagen, a focus on work/life balance, and no dress code.

• An active social environment with monthly events and social clubs.

• A flat organization with open communication, a short path from idea to product, and the creative freedom and trust to create tangible value for our users.

• A highly specialized, international team with room for creativity and professional growth.

• A strong focus on diversity and inclusion, where your ideas are heard and opportunities are available to all.

• Attractive employee benefits, including health insurance, a lunch plan, coffee and fruit, free fitness facilities, and free parking.

• Support for your professional development and personal well-being.

**About You

**We believe you have a solid background in product management and experience working closely with software development teams, preferably on SaaS platforms. You’re curious about how technology works and motivated by making sophisticated tools easy to use.

We also believe you:

• Have 5+ years of experience in product management, taking products or features from discovery to delivery.

• Have a background in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Understand BIM workflows and how building models and their data are used across design, construction, and operations.

• Have a strong understanding of UI/UX principles and can work with designers to evaluate interaction flows, challenge unnecessary complexity, and validate solutions with users.

• Have a working understanding of computer graphics concepts such as 3D geometry, rendering, and model interaction, enabling you to discuss technical trade-offs with engineers.

• Can balance strategic thinking with attention to detail, particularly where usability, model complexity, and performance meet.

• Are comfortable working in agile development environments and prioritizing based on user insights and product outcomes.

• Communicate clearly and fluently in English, both written and spoken.

Experience with IFC, BIM viewers, or other software for working with 3D models would be an advantage.

**Ready for the next step?

**If we have managed to pique your interest, we would love to hear from you. Send us your motivated CV and an application.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please submit your application today.

**About Dalux

**Founded in 2005, Dalux is a Danish Contech company revolutionizing the construction industry with innovative software built on geometric processing and 3D computer graphics. Despite being the world’s second-largest industry, construction remains one of the least digitalized, with only 30% of onsite time spent on actual building tasks. At Dalux, we’re changing this by providing end-to-end solutions that streamline the entire lifecycle of a building—from design and construction to maintenance and eventual demolition—reducing waste, time, and costs.

We stay ahead by using cutting-edge technology, including cloud solutions, drones, computer vision, and AI, to transform how the construction industry works. Over the last five years, we’ve grown by 60% annually and now have over 700 employees across 50+ offices in more than 25 countries. All product development takes place in our Østerbro, Copenhagen office, where we focus on building the future of construction technology. We place great value on our strong social community and close collaboration with colleagues, which is why we primarily work from our Copenhagen location.

If you’re curious to learn more about Dalux and our products, feel free to visit our LinkedIn or website, where you can find videos and descriptions of our events, products, and the work we do.

Experience using AI and emerging technologies to build and automate solutions, including how you tested them before they touched live data.

• 
Experience with Google Tag Manager, GA4, Looker Studio or similar tools.

Experience from a B2B SaaS or scale-up environment.
